name: Daniel Ortega
summary: Ortega, Sandinista leader and Nicaragua's president, denounces global imperialist capitalism and free trade at the UN, demands fair trade and repayment of historical debt, opposed US intervention in Central America, and as president has concentrated power, expelled and denationalised critics and proposed a co-presidency with his wife.

sources.title: Statement by Daniel Ortega Saavedra, President of Nicaragua, UN General Assembly general debate, 62nd session (2007) (UN General Debate Corpus, NIC_62_2007)
sources.author: Daniel Ortega; UN General Debate Corpus (Baturo, Dasandi and Mikhaylov), Harvard Dataverse
sources.usedFor: Global imperialist capitalism, free trade versus fair trade, historical debt, migrants and nuclear energy.

sources.title: Statement by Daniel Ortega Saavedra, President of Nicaragua, UN General Assembly general debate, 42nd session (1987) (UN General Debate Corpus, NIC_42_1987)
sources.author: Daniel Ortega; UN General Debate Corpus (Baturo, Dasandi and Mikhaylov), Harvard Dataverse
sources.usedFor: US aggression and the contras, the Esquipulas agreement, non-alignment, disarmament.

sources.title: World Report 2025: Nicaragua, Human Rights Watch
sources.author: Human Rights Watch
sources.usedFor: Forced exile and citizenship revocation, closure of NGOs and universities, the proposed co-presidency and coordination of other branches, persecution of the Church.

sources.title: Nicaragua: A Country Study (Library of Congress Federal Research Division, 1993), PDF copy on the USC Latin America site
sources.author: Library of Congress Federal Research Division (ed. Tim Merrill)
sources.usedFor: The Sandinista government's Agrarian Reform Law (1981), nationalisations, the 1982 Law of National Emergency, the 1985 state of emergency and the censorship of La Prensa.

sources.title: Nicaragua's Ortega: President for life?, Christian Science Monitor, 29 January 2014 (Tim Rogers)
sources.author: Christian Science Monitor
sources.usedFor: The January 2014 constitutional reform clearing the way for Ortega's indefinite re-election.

sources.title: Daniel Ortega, Wikipedia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Orientation to his career as Sandinista leader and President (1985-90, 2007-), used to locate the primary texts.

notFound.work: Ortega's 2006 abortion ban, Law 1040 (2020) and the 2021 election record, and the 2025 constitutional reform as enacted

tried.how: the 1981, 1983 and 1984 speeches are in the corpus and were searched by theme (revolution, aggression, non-alignment) but add nothing beyond the 1987 text cited
only HRW and press summaries turned up for the constitutional reforms

notes: First audit. Read by theme his 2007 and 1987 UN General Assembly speeches (and searched those of 1981, 1983 and 1984) and Human Rights Watch's World Report 2025 chapter on Nicaragua (his government's acts). MediaSum hits for 'Daniel Ortega' mix the Nicaraguan president with an Arizona immigration attorney and a National Council of La Raza spokesperson (different people, not used); his own words there ('we have to restore order', 'armed conspiracy financed from abroad') are translated and state no position on a test statement. His 1980s government's acts are cited from the Library of Congress country study (Agrarian Reform Law, nationalisations, the 1982 and 1985 states of emergency, censorship of La Prensa) and the 2014 reform from the Christian Science Monitor; the 2006 abortion ban, Law 1040 and the 2021 election were searched and not found in an open page I could open, and are not answered. The countrystudies.us mirror refused automated access (403) and was not used.
